notes: The two rows come from opposite directions, and that is the point. Bambara month names are French, respelled to Bambara phonology by the 1967 orthography — zanwuye for janvier, awirili for avril, ɔkutɔburu for octobre — because the Gregorian calendar arrived with the colonial administration and the school. The weekday names arrived centuries earlier with Islam and are Arabic worn down by Manding mouths: ntɛnɛn from al-ithnayn, tarata from ath-thulatha, araba from al-arbaʿa, alamisa from al-khamis, juma from al-jumʿa the day of congregation, sibiri from as-sabt. Only kari, Sunday, belongs to neither borrowing. Bambara has no v, so janvier cannot keep its v and takes w; it has no capital letter convention for months, so these stay lowercase mid-sentence. Dates run day-first, as in France, and the two dotless short forms are the months whose names are already short enough not to abbreviate.
